_comment: Roll-a-Day: Retirement Edition. The reader rolls a die for a morning plan (1-6) and again for an afternoon plan (1-6) and puts the two together: 36 possible days. Nobody checks the 36 pairings one by one, so every activity is held to one shape that makes any morning combine with any afternoon: about half a day or less, self-contained (never continuing or depending on the other half), no mealtime, no whole-day or overnight plan, and nothing belonging to the other half of the day (morningBanned / afternoonBanned) or to the evening (anySideBanned). No two activities on a page share a word of substance (softWords aside: who and where, not what), so no day doubles up. Variety is structural: each side takes six different kinds (the four coreKinds plus two extraKinds, the focus's boost first), every activity gets its own facet and flavour, shuffled by seed. exclusiveTerms keep the table open to everyone: nothing strenuous, no car, no golf course or beach house assumed. Idea shape, safety and meaning-level repeats reuse the Bucket List's gates (bucket-list/prompt.json).
